change_triggers: Export API or queued-job contract change

constraints: No runtime action is included in this source-observed example.

scope.description: All first-party source, configuration, and supplied documents in the fictional example application.

limitations.statement: Runtime execution and third-party internals are outside this source-observed example scope.

system_purpose.statement: The fictional application lets authenticated tenants create asynchronous exports of their own records.

overall_assessment.statement: The source path exposes a high-risk tenant-isolation decision that requires mitigation and authorized validation; all declared source scope is dispositioned.

model_status_rationale.statement: Every admitted component, high-signal flow, boundary, control, privacy lane, decision, and source coverage item in the example is reviewed; runtime execution was not in scope.

assurance_limitations.statement: The planned access-control test has not run, so exploitability and deployed enforcement remain unverified.

description.statement: A tenant user can request an export after authentication.
Export records contain tenant-owned personal and business data.
The create-export route accepts a request and enqueues export work.
The worker consumes queued export jobs and selects records for the requested tenant.
Completed export objects are written to a dedicated object store.
Tenant-controlled clients are outside the application trust boundary.
The export API runs in the application service zone.
The export worker runs with background-processing privileges.
Tenant export data and completed objects reside in the restricted data zone.
An untrusted tenant client crosses into the API zone when creating an export.

trust_change.statement: Authentication establishes a principal, but request values remain attacker controlled.

description.statement: The API passes an export job into the privileged worker zone.

trust_change.statement: The queued tenant value becomes input to a privileged data-selection process.

description.statement: The worker crosses into restricted storage to read records and write the export object.

trust_change.statement: Worker-supplied tenant scope determines which restricted records can enter the export.

description.statement: An authenticated request creates a job that a worker resolves into a stored tenant export.

trigger.statement: A tenant user submits a create-export request.

input.statement: The request contains export parameters including a tenant identifier.

operation.statement: The client submits an authenticated export request.

principal.statement: Authentication associates the request with a tenant user principal.

tenant.statement: The request also carries a caller-supplied tenant identifier.

roles.statement: The established principal has the tenant_user role.

trust_basis.statement: The principal comes from authentication middleware; request fields remain untrusted.

outcome.statement: The route requires an authenticated principal.

operation.statement: The API serializes export parameters into the worker job.

principal.statement: The job is created on behalf of the authenticated tenant user.

tenant.statement: The queued tenant identifier is copied from the request rather than shown as server derived.

roles.statement: The worker processes the request under its service privileges.

trust_basis.statement: The worker trusts the job producer but must still bind tenant scope to the initiating principal.

outcome.statement: Source review did not establish server-derived tenant binding before enqueue.

operation.statement: The worker selects tenant records and writes the completed export object.

principal.statement: The worker uses a privileged service identity for data access.

tenant.statement: The worker query scope comes from the queued tenant identifier.

roles.statement: The worker service can read exportable tenant records and write export objects.

trust_basis.statement: Correct isolation depends on the queued tenant value being bound to the initiating principal.

outcome.statement: The worker query uses the job tenant value; a separate principal-to-tenant check was not located.

sink_or_final_state.statement: A tenant-scoped export object is expected to be stored for later download.

side_effects.statement: The asynchronous job and completed object persist until cleanup or retention processing.

statement.statement: A tenant user must never cause another tenant's records to be selected or included in an export.

description.statement: Authentication middleware establishes a tenant user before the export route runs.

rationale.statement: The middleware invocation is visible at the export route, although authentication alone does not bind tenant scope.

description.statement: Tenant scope should be derived from the authenticated principal before enqueue and preserved through worker selection.

rationale.statement: The source shows tenant values crossing both enforcement points, but authorized runtime evidence is not available.

threats.title: Request-controlled tenant scope reaches export selection

goal.statement: An authenticated tenant user attempts to include another tenant's records in an export.

preconditions.statement: The attacker has a normal authenticated tenant account.
The attacker can influence the tenant identifier accepted by the export route.

action.statement: Submit an export request containing a foreign synthetic tenant identifier.
Cause the API to preserve the foreign tenant identifier in the worker job.
Cause the privileged worker to select foreign tenant records and write them into the export.

contradiction_checks.statement: The export route's authentication middleware was located and narrows the actor to an authenticated user.
Review of the route and worker call sites did not locate a separate server-derived principal-to-tenant binding.
Deployment topology was reviewed for a compensating tenant enforcement point, but none is specified in the supplied configuration.

business_impact.statement: A successful path could disclose restricted personal and business records across tenants.

rationale.statement: An authenticated user can reach the export flow with low complexity; if request-supplied tenant scope reaches the privileged worker, restricted cross-tenant data could enter an export.
The complete source path is observed, while exploitability remains untested because runtime execution is outside the example scope.

next_action.statement: Derive tenant scope from the authenticated principal before enqueue and revalidate it in the worker query.

rationale.statement: Two independent enforcement points prevent request and job tampering from becoming privileged cross-tenant selection.
Server-derived tenant scope at both enqueue and worker query would reduce likelihood, while implementation and regression evidence would still be required.

attack_paths.title: Tenant request to cross-tenant export object

preconditions.statement: A disposable tenant user can create exports in an authorized test environment.
Two synthetic tenants contain owner-attributed marker records.

condition.statement: The actor authenticates normally and submits an altered tenant identifier.

outcome.statement: The API receives attacker-influenced tenant scope under a valid principal.

condition.statement: The API preserves the altered tenant identifier in the job payload.

outcome.statement: The privileged worker receives tenant scope not yet proven to be principal bound.

condition.statement: The worker query accepts the altered job tenant scope.

outcome.statement: Foreign synthetic tenant data could be placed into the completed export object.

final_impact.statement: The requesting tenant could receive restricted records belonging to another tenant.

rationale.statement: All attack-path hops are connected in source, but the decisive tenant-binding behavior still requires an authorized test.
Source evidence supports the connected path; runtime success or denial has not been observed.

question.statement: Where must tenant scope be bound to the authenticated principal for asynchronous exports?

description.statement: Derive tenant scope at the API and carry a signed or integrity-protected principal context to the worker, which revalidates before querying.

security_effect.statement: Both privilege transitions enforce the same principal-to-tenant invariant.

tradeoffs.statement: Requires a versioned job contract and worker-side policy code.

description.statement: Continue passing a caller-supplied tenant identifier and rely only on API validation.

security_effect.statement: Leaves the worker dependent on upstream correctness and weakens defense across the asynchronous boundary.

tradeoffs.statement: Requires less implementation change but retains a single enforcement point.

recommendation.statement: Select the principal-derived, worker-revalidated tenant context design.

rationale.statement: The recommended option enforces tenant isolation before both job creation and privileged data selection.

validation_tests.title: Verify principal-bound tenant scope across the export worker

hypothesis.statement: A tenant A principal cannot cause tenant B synthetic records to be selected or stored by changing request or job tenant identifiers.

preconditions: Explicit authorization for the isolated local test target
Disposable tenant A and tenant B accounts
Synthetic owner-attributed marker records for both tenants
fixture_setup: Create tenant A record TENANT_A_MARKER and tenant B record TENANT_B_MARKER
Authenticate as the disposable tenant A user
Clear prior export jobs and objects for both fixtures

description.statement: A normal tenant A export should complete with only tenant A synthetic records.

steps: Request an export as tenant A without altering tenant context
Wait for the bounded job to complete
Inspect the synthetic export and authoritative worker query trace

expected_signals.observation: Tenant A export contains only the synthetic TENANT_A_MARKER record.
expected_signals.interpretation: The normal flow works and preserves tenant A ownership.

evidence_to_collect: Redacted request identifier and job identifier
Worker tenant-scope trace containing only synthetic identifiers
Hash and owner labels of the completed synthetic export

objective.statement: Attempt to make tenant A's export select tenant B's synthetic records by altering tenant context.

steps: Submit the same export request while substituting tenant B's synthetic identifier
If authorized, inspect the queued job without modifying production-like state
Wait for the bounded job outcome and inspect the synthetic export

attacker_success_signal.observation: Tenant A receives the synthetic TENANT_B_MARKER in the completed export.
attacker_success_signal.interpretation: The modeled cross-tenant disclosure path succeeded in the authorized fixture.

expected_denial_signal.observation: The request is rejected or the completed export contains only TENANT_A_MARKER.
expected_denial_signal.interpretation: Tenant isolation prevented tenant B data from entering tenant A's export.

steps: Inspect the API-derived tenant context for the altered request
Inspect the worker query scope for the resulting job
Compare both values with the authenticated tenant A principal

control_success_signal.observation: Worker query parameters contain the server-derived tenant A identifier only.
control_success_signal.interpretation: The expected principal-bound tenant control held at the privileged query.

control_failure_signal.observation: Worker query parameters contain the request-supplied tenant B identifier.
control_failure_signal.interpretation: The expected worker-side tenant control did not hold.

evidence_to_collect: Authoritative worker query parameters with synthetic tenant labels
Completed export hash and synthetic owner labels

constraints: Do not target production, third parties, real tenants, or real accounts
Run one bounded export at a time
Use only synthetic markers and redacted evidence
stop_conditions: Stop if the target revision differs from the modeled revision
Stop if any non-synthetic record appears
Stop if queue or object-store cleanup cannot be verified
evidence_handling: Store only redacted identifiers and hashes
Do not preserve credentials, tokens, export contents, or customer data

steps: Remove or expire both bounded test jobs
Delete the synthetic marker records and disposable tenant accounts

verification_signals.observation: Both synthetic export objects and queued jobs are absent after cleanup.
verification_signals.interpretation: The authorized test left no fixture data or pending work.

rationale.statement: The steps have discriminating oracles, but the test remains unexecuted until authorization is granted.
